sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198], but the path was a step change rather than a steady climb.
Revenue grew 89.1% in FY2021 to $16.1 billion [F6][D241], with REGEN-COV US sales of $5.83 billion adding 66.4pp [S48][D582], following the September 2021 agreement to supply the US government [P39].
Revenue then fell 24.3% in FY2022 [D292] as REGEN-COV US sales went to $0 [S49], because those sales and their cost of goods did not recur [P33].
Since FY2022 revenue has grown at a 5.6% three-year CAGR [D767], and FY2025 growth was only 1.0% [D440].
Collaboration revenue rose 21.0% in FY2025, adding 9.0pp to growth, and is now 51.1% of revenue [D522][D523][D521].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits grew 33.6% to $5.24 billion, driven by higher Dupixent sales [S52][D591][P9].
Net product sales fell 17.3%, subtracting 9.3pp from growth [D506][D507].

US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% to $2.75 billion on lower volumes, competition, compounded bevacizumab and a lower net price [S43][D577][P10], while EYLEA HD grew 36.3% to $1.64 billion on higher volumes [S64][D613][P11].
Operating costs outgrew revenue by 4.4pp, so operating income fell 10.3% [D464][D441].
Net income rose 2.1% but diluted EPS rose 8.2%, because the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D442][D444][D459].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 is the window low, against a median of 34.6% and a high of 55.7% [F30][D749][D751][D750].
The FY2025 margin fell 3.2pp [D453]: R&D lowered it by 4.7pp [D465], while SG&A contributed +2.0pp [D466].
SG&A fell 8.6% mainly on lower charitable contributions to a patient assistance fund [D456][P5]; the passages cited do not explain why R&D rose 14.0% to $5.85 billion [D455][X34].

The largest move was FY2022, down 16.7pp, with R&D costing 11.4pp and SG&A 6.0pp [D305][D318][D319]; SG&A rose on headcount and Libtayo commercialization [P34], and the cited filings do not explain the R&D line that year.
Net margin of 31.4% sits 6.5pp above operating margin of 24.9% because other income reached $1.65 billion, up from $789 million [F50][F30][X117][X116]; the pack gives no cause for that rise.
Operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income, and free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x, against a window median of 0.88x [F80][D428][F100][D429][D763].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% compares with a window median of 26.4% [D425][D757].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898 million, which is 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D447][F90][D424][D430].
The FY2023 10-K said it expected continued significant capital expenditures over the next several years [P19].
In FY2025, stock-based compensation was 20.0% of operating cash flow [D431].
Net cash of $16.9 billion, up from $15.9 billion, equals 117.7% of revenue, the 100th percentile among eight biopharma peers whose median is -50.7% [D434][D385][D435][D780][D781].
Debt is $1.99 billion and the current ratio is 4.13x [D433][F180].
Buybacks plus dividends were $3.81 billion, 93.3% of free cash flow against 71.0% in FY2024 [D436][D437][D388]; this includes the first dividends in the window, $370 million [X140].
Return on average equity of 14.9% ranks at the 25th percentile of eight peers, whose median is 38.7% [D439][D784][D785].
Operating margin fell four years in a row, 30.7pp in total, from 55.7% to 24.9% [R1][F26][F30].
R&D at 40.8% of revenue is the largest cost drag and the margin has not yet stabilised [D420][D465].
US EYLEA sales have fallen three years running and were 19.2% of revenue in FY2025 [D571][D574][D577][D576].
EYLEA HD has only partly replaced the lost sales, so the base the collaboration income sits on is shrinking [S46][D507].
Capital return took 93.3% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D437].
The buyback pace leaves little cushion if free cash flow weakens further [D436].
Data quality: FY2018 revenue is $5.15 billion in the table against $6.71 billion first reported, and FY2019 is $6.56 billion against $7.86 billion [R2][F3][X3][F4][X4].

I therefore draw no conclusion from FY2018 or FY2019 growth or margins; the two low-severity recasts of FY2021 R&D and FY2020 receivables are dropped because the pack uses the first-reported values [R3][R4].
Operating margin below the window low of 24.9% in the FY2026 10-K would confirm continued compression, and a margin above it would reverse the trend [D749].
Combined US EYLEA HD and EYLEA sales below $4.38 billion in the FY2026 10-K would show erosion outrunning the HD transition [S46].
R&D as a share of revenue above the window high of 42.2% in the FY2026 10-K would extend the cost pressure, while a reading below FY2025's 40.8% would ease it [D759][D420].
Buybacks plus dividends above 93.3% of free cash flow in the FY2026 10-K would signal payout outpacing cash generation [D437].
